title: Bangladesh Moves Toward $2.3B Chinese J-10CE Fighter Deal as Seoul Nuclear Debate Swells to 65% Support
subhead: Bangladesh is finalizing a draft agreement for up to 24 Chinese J-10CE fighters and attack helicopters, citing the jet's disputed Operation Sindoor record, while a Gallup poll shows 65% of South Koreans now back an indigenous nuclear arsenal amid Washington's reduced drill posture. Poland's government is publicly split over hosting US nuclear warheads.

sections.heading: Bangladesh Finalizing $2.3B J-10CE Purchase From China
sections.body: Bangladesh is moving closer to a formal fighter-jet deal with China, with a government panel now preparing a draft agreement for the purchase of J-10CE fighters and attack helicopters, adviser to the prime minister Zahed Ur Rahman said this week, per Reuters. Local media estimate up to 24 aircraft worth about $2.3 billion, payable over a decade, though Rahman did not disclose jet numbers, value or delivery timeline, saying those would be settled through negotiation. Rahman told Reuters that Dhaka has taken note of the J-10CE's reported performance during Operation Sindoor, last year's India-Pakistan clashes, a claim India disputes. Pakistan remains the only confirmed foreign operator of the J-10CE, the export variant of China's J-10C multirole fighter.
sections.whyItMatters: A combat-flavored Chinese fighter entering service on Bangladesh's border with India deepens Beijing's hold on Dhaka's defense procurement, which already spans naval vessels, tanks and missiles. It also widens New Delhi's concern about Chinese hardware operating on both its eastern and western flanks simultaneously.

sections.heading: Poland's Government Splits in Public Over Hosting US Nuclear Warheads
sections.body: Deputy Defence Minister Paweł Zalewski told reporters after meeting US Under Secretary of Defense Elbridge Colby in Brussels on August 27 that Poland wants 'several' permanent US bases, not just one, with a Colby office official to visit soon to review proposed locations. But Zalewski also said Poland 'does not want to have nuclear warheads on its territory,' even as it seeks to participate in NATO nuclear deterrence — a declaration that triggered an immediate backlash, Brussels Signal reports. President Karol Nawrocki's foreign-policy chief Marcin Przydacz called the remarks 'bizarre and absurd,' while former National Security Bureau chief Gen. Stanisław Koziej called it 'an incomprehensible strategic error in the field of deterrence.' Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz intervened on X to clarify that Poland 'remains steadfastly interested' in the NATO Nuclear Sharing program and is in talks on the European nuclear umbrella; Zalewski later said Poland secured access to the dual-capable aircraft (DCA) program, calling storing warheads 'neither possible nor desirable.'
sections.whyItMatters: The public rupture exposes a real split between Poland's Tusk government and the Nawrocki-allied presidency over NATO's nuclear-sharing architecture, just as Washington's 'NATO 3.0' review pushes Europe toward carrying its own conventional defense. How Warsaw resolves the nuclear question will shape its standing on the alliance's eastern flank.

sections.heading: US Navy Awards $76.6B in Submarine Contracts Even as GAO Warns of Readiness Crisis
sections.body: The US Navy on Wednesday awarded $76.6 billion in contract modifications to Huntington Ingalls' Newport News Shipbuilding and General Dynamics Electric Boat covering nine additional Block VI Virginia-class and five Build II Columbia-class submarines, plus shipyard infrastructure investment, per Yahoo Finance. Newport News will act as delivery yard for six of the Virginia-class boats and build six module sections per Columbia. Days earlier, a Government Accountability Office report (Aug 27) found the Navy has lost 15,000 operational days on attack submarines to maintenance backlogs and shipyard delays, costing an estimated $3.4 billion in sustainment — with a warning that 15 subs could enter inactive idle status between FY2026 and FY2030 at a further cost exceeding $3.1 billion.
sections.whyItMatters: The pairing lays bare the central tension in the US submarine program: record procurement money is flowing to build 14 new boats while the existing 44-ship attack-submarine force ages pier-side awaiting maintenance. Industrial capacity and shipyard throughput, not contracts, are the binding constraint on US undersea power.

sections.heading: Two-Thirds of South Koreans Back an Indigenous Nuclear Arsenal
sections.body: A Gallup Korea poll conducted August 25-27 of 1,001 respondents found 65 percent support South Korea developing its own nuclear weapons, against 30 percent opposed, TASS reports citing Yonhap. Support runs across the political spectrum — 78 percent among conservatives backing the opposition People Power Party and 60 percent among ruling Democratic Party voters. Thirty-nine percent believe a military conflict could break out on the peninsula. The poll lands amid heightened sensitivity after President Trump on August 16 ordered a reduction in the scale and timeline of US-South Korea joint drills while recalling his 'good relations' with Kim Jong Un, stoking fears Washington may shift from denuclearization toward arms control. Seoul has reaffirmed it still seeks a nuclear-free peninsula, and separately confirmed South Korea, Japan and the US will hold a North Korea-focused nuclear missile drill September 9-11, per Reuters.
sections.whyItMatters: At 65 percent, public appetite for an independent South Korean deterrent has moved from fringe to mainstream and is now cross-partisan — a durable shift in political baseline. It pressures both Seoul's non-proliferation stance and Washington's extended deterrence posture at a moment when the US is visibly trimming its peninsula exercises.

sections.heading: India Nears $9B TKMS Submarine Deal as German Frigate Costs Spiral
sections.body: Germany's thyssenkrupp Marine Systems (TKMS) is closing in on a roughly $9 billion contract under India's Project 75(I) to build six conventional AIP-equipped submarines with Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders in Mumbai, including technology transfer, per industry reporting. The deal would rank among TKMS's largest orders and bolsters a global pipeline that includes Canada's Class 212CD program and a cooperation pact with Spain's Navantia. The momentum is complicated domestically: Berlin has halted the F126 frigate program over cost overruns, and the separate F127 air-defense frigate has escalated from an estimated €26 billion to over €40 billion for eight vessels, per a Spiegel report TKMS disputes — driven partly by eight US-built Aegis combat-system sets at $11.9 billion plus $3.5 billion in SM-6 and SM-2 missiles. Germany would become the first international user of the SPY-6(V1) radar.
sections.whyItMatters: This is the clearest sign yet of a mature German shipbuilding export strategy colliding with domestic cost discipline: TKMS's expansion into India, Canada and Europe is underwriting its growth even as Germany's own frigate programs face political scrutiny and possible redirection toward cheaper MEKO A-200 boats.

sections.heading: Ukraine Fields Alexa Spatium Jet-Powered Interceptor Drone
sections.body: Ukraine's defense ministry confirmed a new domestically built turbojet interceptor, dubbed Alexa Spatium, has entered military service, engineered to hunt Russian Geran-3, Geran-4 and Geran-5 kamikaze drones and the Shahed-131 loitering munition, The Register reports. The compact 1.5-by-1.7-meter aircraft is fired from a portable catapult near the front line and is designed to return home if it misses its target, fitted with thermobaric, shaped-charge, fragmentation or high-explosive warheads depending on the threat. It uses an electro-optical camera paired with infrared sensing. Britain introduced a comparable turbojet interceptor, Skyhammer from Cambridge Aerospace, earlier this year. Neither system offers protection against ballistic missiles, a gap underscored by the thinning of US-supplied Patriot stocks.
sections.whyItMatters: The Alexa Spatium confirms the cost-driver logic of modern counter-drone warfare: cheap, reusable jet interceptors are becoming the preferred answer to swarms of one-way attack drones, letting militaries preserve expensive surface-to-air missiles for the ballistic threat no drone can stop.

bottomLine: Today's defense picture is defined by procurement decisions and political signals rather than a single headline event. Bangladesh's advance toward a $2.3 billion Chinese J-10CE deal — citing last year's India-Pakistan clashes — shows Beijing's combat-flavored hardware, and its marketing after Operation Sindoor, is gaining buyers across South Asia. In the alliance sphere, Poland's government publicly split over whether to host US nuclear warheads just as Washington's NATO 3.0 review pushes Europe to lead its own defense, while a Gallup poll found 65 percent of South Koreans now favor an indigenous nuclear arsenal amid reduced US drill posture. The US poured a record $76.6 billion into new submarines as its GAO warns the existing fleet is losing operational days faster than the yards can fix them, and India moved closer to a $9 billion German submarine deal even as Berlin wrestles with its own ballooning frigate costs. The through-line: demand for capable, affordable and politically sustainable defense is reshaping procurement in both hemispheres — from reusable jet interceptors on the Ukrainian frontline to the nuclear debates now opening in Warsaw and Seoul.
sources: Reuters, Republic World, Moneycontrol, FIRSTPOST, Brussels Signal, Yahoo Finance, Stars & Stripes, TASS (via Yonhap/Gallup Korea), UPI, Ad-Hoc News, The Register (via Yahoo)
